title: How Specialty Practices Recover $14,100 per Physician in Unpaid Patient Balances
summary: Patients pay 36% of specialty care costs, and nearly 8% goes unpaid. See what recovering balances is worth per physician and how to collect more.
body_markdown:
Patient responsibility (also called a patient balance or patient-due balance) is the share of a bill a patient owes after insurance: deductibles, coinsurance, copays and self-pay. Patients now pay 36% of specialty care costs, and Prosper AI's[2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) values recovering unpaid balances at $14,100 per physician a year.


A balance that isn't collected at the front desk turns into a statement, then a second statement, then a third. By then the patient has questions about the charge, and a statement can't answer them.


Nearly 8% of what patients owe goes unpaid, according to the Growth Report. Recovering it is the smallest of the 4 revenue levers, and it grows every time patients take on more of the bill. For a 20-physician practice, it's worth about $282K a year for care the practice already delivered.


## **TL;DR**


- Patients pay 36% of the cost of their care at specialty practices, and 55% in dermatology.
- Nearly 8% of what patients owe goes unpaid.
- Practices collect about 72% of copays at the time of service, but only about 27% of other patient-due balances.
- Recovering unpaid balances is worth an estimated $14,100 per physician per year, rising to $24K in dermatology.
- In a randomized comparison at one multi-location dermatology practice, AI reminder calls recovered 48% more outstanding balances than standard follow-up.


## How much of the bill do patients pay at specialty practices?


Patients pay an average of 36% of the cost of their care at specialty practices, and 55% in dermatology, according to Prosper AI's[2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) . The figures come from more than 5 million calls Prosper AI has completed with providers and payers.


That share includes every dollar insurance doesn't cover:


Balance type What it is


Copay A fixed amount per visit, usually known before the patient arrives


Deductible What the patient pays before the plan starts covering care


Coinsurance A percentage of the allowed amount the patient owes after the deductible


Self-pay Services the plan doesn't cover, or patients without coverage


Copays are the easy part. Deductibles and coinsurance often aren't final until the claim is processed, which is why most of the balance gets billed after the visit.


The pressure shows up beyond billing too. In an[August 2026 MGMA Stat poll](https://www.mgma.com/mgma-stat/about-1-in-3-medical-groups-see-higher-no-shows-in-2026-as-patients-face-higher-costs) , 32% of medical groups reported more no-shows than in 2025, and the poll tied the rise to higher costs for patients.


## How much patient revenue goes uncollected?


Nearly 8% of what patients owe goes unpaid according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report. Most of the rest gets collected late, after rounds of statements and staff follow-up.


The gap opens at the front desk. In an[MGMA Stat poll](https://www.mgma.com/mgma-stat/about-1-in-3-medical-groups-see-higher-no-shows-in-2026-as-patients-face-higher-costs) , practices reported collecting about 72% of copayments at the time of service, but only 26.83% of other patient-due balances. Everything left over moves into the billing queue, where each balance means more statements, more calls and a higher chance it's never paid.


It's getting harder, too. In a 2025 survey cited in the Growth Report, 29% of medical practices said recovering outstanding patient balances had become more difficult over the past year, compared with 26% that saw improvement.

Recovering unpaid patient balances is worth an estimated $14,100 a year for the average specialty physician, according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report. That's 3.2% of the $445K in patient-paid revenue a physician brings in:

## Why don't statements and payment portals collect the balance?


Because a patient who hasn't paid usually has a question first, and statements and portals can't answer it. Why do I owe this? Didn't my insurance cover it? Can I pay over time?


A statement tells the patient what they owe. It can't explain what insurance paid, walk through the deductible or set up a payment plan. A portal can take a payment, but only from a patient who logs in already ready to pay. So the questions go to the billing office by phone, and the billing office is working the same aging list it was last month.


Staff calls work when someone has time to make them. At most specialty practices, the people who could make those calls are also covering a front desk that already[misses 18% of inbound calls](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/missed-calls-specialty-practices) during office hours.


## What happens when patients get a call instead of another statement?


They pay more of what they owe. At one multi-location dermatology practice, AI reminder calls recovered 48% more outstanding patient balances than the practice's standard follow-up, according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report.


The practice ran a randomized comparison. Households whose balances had reached a third billing statement got either AI reminder calls or the usual statements and follow-up. The calls explained the balance, answered questions about charges and insurance, and offered a payment link, a payment plan or a transfer to the billing team.

Figures are the cumulative share of outstanding balances paid over about 50 days after that statement. Source: Prosper internal data, published in the 2026 Growth Report.


## Statements vs. text-to-pay vs. staff calls vs. AI billing calls: which collects more?


The approach that collects the most answers the patient's questions about the charge and offers a way to pay in the same conversation. Here's how the 4 common approaches compare:


Statements (mail or email) Text-to-pay links Staff billing calls Prosper AI billing calls


Explains what insurance paid On paper only No Yes Yes


Answers questions about the charge No No Yes Yes, with a transfer to billing for disputes


Offers a payment plan Sometimes, by phone Rarely Yes Yes, within your policy


Takes payment in the moment No Yes, by link Yes Yes, by link or transfer


Reaches patients who ignore mail No Yes, if they open texts Yes, if staff has time Yes


Staff time required Low to send, high to follow up Low High Exceptions only


Scales across locations Yes Yes Add staff per location Yes


The second row decides it. A patient with an unanswered question about their bill tends to wait, and every week a balance ages makes it harder to collect.


## What should specialty groups look for in patient billing outreach software?


The best patient billing outreach software for a multi-location specialty group explains each balance using claim and benefits data, answers the patient's questions and offers a way to pay on the same call. Check these 6 things before you shortlist:


1. **Balance explanations from claim data.** It should tell the patient what was billed, what insurance paid and why they owe the rest.
2. **Insurance and coverage answers.** Patients ask about deductibles and coinsurance before they pay. It should answer those questions accurately.
3. **Payment links and plans within your policy.** It should send a link during the call and offer only the plans your billing policy allows.
4. **Escalation to your billing team.** Disputes, hardship requests and anything unusual should go to a person, with a call summary.
5. **Write-back to your PM or EHR system.** Call outcomes, promises to pay and payments should land where your billers work.
6. **Security paperwork.** A signed BAA and a current SOC 2 Type II report.


## How do you collect more patient balances across multiple locations?


Tell patients their cost before the visit, collect what you can at check-in, and call before a balance ages into its third statement. Here's how to set it up in 5 steps:


1. **Share the estimate before the visit.** The[benefits check that prevents denials](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/preventable-claim-denials-specialty-practices) also gives you the patient's deductible, coinsurance and copay. Tell the patient what they'll likely owe when you confirm the appointment.
2. **Collect at the time of service.** Ask for the copay and any known balance at check-in, with a card-on-file or payment link option.
3. **Call before the third statement.** Once a balance has gone through a statement or two, a call that explains it and offers a way to pay outperforms another envelope.
4. **Make paying easy.** Offer a payment link, a payment plan within your policy, and a fast route to your billing team for disputes.
5. **Track it weekly, by location.** Watch 3 numbers: the share of patient responsibility collected at the time of service, the share of aged balances recovered, and days in patient A/R.


Start with balances that have reached a second or third statement at one location, measure the recovery rate against your usual follow-up, then roll out the same rules everywhere.


## How do the 4 revenue levers work together?


Together, the 4 levers in Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report add up to an estimated $125,000 in additional revenue per physician a year. Each one also feeds the next.


Lever What it fixes Opportunity per physician / year


1. Convert missed calls Patient calls that never get answered $44,800


2. Re-engage existing patients Follow-ups that slip or never happen $37,400


3. Prevent avoidable denials Front-end errors that get claims denied $28,500


4. Recover the patient responsibility Balances that go unpaid after the visit $14,100


Total $125,000


The link between them is the appointment itself. When a visit is booked with coverage confirmed and the patient's cost shared upfront, the claim is less likely to be denied, and the Growth Report finds patients who know their costs are more likely to show up and pay after the visit. A practice that's easy to reach and clear about cost also stands out to new patients, which brings the cycle back to Lever 1.


## Frequently asked questions


**What is patient responsibility in medical billing?**


Patient responsibility is the part of a medical bill a patient owes after insurance pays its share. It includes deductibles, coinsurance, copays and self-pay charges for services the plan doesn't cover.


**How much of their care do patients pay for at specialty practices?**


Patients pay an average of 36% of the cost of their care at specialty practices, and 55% in dermatology, according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report.


**What percentage of patient balances go unpaid?**


About 7.9% of what patients owe goes unpaid, according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report. Practices collect about 72% of copays at the time of service but only 26.83% of other patient-due balances, according to an MGMA Stat poll.


**Which specialty has the most patient balance revenue to recover?**


Dermatology, at an estimated $24,000 per physician a year, according to Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report. Ophthalmology follows at $15,000, then primary care at $14,000, OB/GYN and orthopedics at $13,000 each, and gastroenterology at $12,000.


**How can practices collect more patient balances?**


Share the patient's estimated cost before the visit, collect copays and known balances at check-in, and call patients before a balance reaches its third statement. At one multi-location dermatology practice, AI reminder calls recovered 48% more outstanding balances than standard follow-up.


**Can AI call patients about their balance?**


Yes. Prosper AI calls patients about outstanding balances, explains the charges, answers questions about insurance, and offers a payment link, a payment plan or a transfer to your billing team.


**Is AI patient billing outreach HIPAA compliant?**


It can be, and you should[ask every vendor for proof](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/is-ai-hipaa-compliant-healthcare-guide) . Prosper AI is HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, and signs a BAA with every customer.
